slot.brief: Battery of known emf and internal resistance connected across external resistor; find terminal voltage, current and power delivered — simple two-step circuit analysis.

stem: A cell of emf $12\ \text{V}$ and internal resistance $1\ \Omega$ is connected to a $5\ \Omega$ resistor. What are the current, terminal voltage and power delivered to the resistor?

verdicts.working: Total resistance is 5 + 1 = 6 Ω, so I = 12/6 = 2 A. Terminal voltage = IR = 10 V; resistor power = I²R = 20 W.

working:
$I=\dfrac{\mathcal{E}}{R+r}=\dfrac{12}{5+1}=2\ \text{A}$
$V=IR=2(5)=10\ \text{V}$
$P=I^2R=2^2(5)=20\ \text{W}$

Independent check: Total resistance is 5 + 1 = 6 Ω, so I = 12/6 = 2 A. Terminal voltage = IR = 10 V; resistor power = I²R = 20 W.
solution:
The current is determined by the total resistance, including the cell’s internal resistance:
$$I=\frac{\mathcal{E}}{R+r}=\frac{12}{5+1}=2\ \text{A}$$
Thus, $V=IR=10\ \text{V}$ and $P=I^2R=20\ \text{W}$.
